question: Who was the founder of the Brahmo Samaj in the nineteenth century?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Raja Ram Mohan Roy.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Hinduism's Brahmo Samaj** was a monotheistic group.
 
• Through gatherings of **Bengalis in Calcutta in 1828,** the movement had its start.
 
• The** adoration of the Eternal God **was the main goal of the** Brahmo Samaj**. It was opposed to sacrifices, ceremonies, and priesthood. It placed a strong emphasis on** scripture reading, meditation, and prayer.**
 
• The** samaj has had great success** with its social reform initiatives, but it has never attracted a sizable amount of support from the **general public. **
 
• One of the founders of the **Brahmo Sabha,** the forerunner of the **Brahmo Samaj**, a social-religious reform movement in the Indian subcontinent, was** Ram Mohan Roy. **The Mughal emperor **Akbar II gave him the title "Raja."**​ 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **​Narendranath Datta,** often known as **Swami Vivekananda, **was an Indian Hindu monk, philosopher, and writer. He was the foremost pupil of the Indian **spiritual Ramakrishna in the 19th century.**
 
• Born** Gadadhar Chattopadhyaya**, **Ramakrishna Paramahamsa**, was an Indian Hindu mystic and religious figure who lived in **Bengal in the 19th century.**
 
• **Ishwar Chandra Bandyopadhyay,** better known by his given name **Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar CIE**, was a nineteenth-century Indian educator and social reformer. He made a lot of effort to **modernise and streamline Bengali literature**.
